question_text: A 32-year-old woman comes to her doctor’s office with abdominal distention, diffuse abdominal pain, and a history of 10–12 bowel movements a day for the last week. She was diagnosed with Crohn’s disease 3 years ago. Today, vitals are normal. Her abdomen is mildly distended and diffusely tender to palpation. A CT scan shows evidence of a fistula and strictures located in the last 30 cm of her ileum. A resection of the affected portion of the bowel is scheduled. What changes in bile metabolism are expected in this patient post-procedure?

Question: A 32-year-old woman comes to her doctor’s office with abdominal distention, diffuse abdominal pain, and a history of 10–12 bowel movements a day for the last week. She was diagnosed with Crohn’s disease 3 years ago. Today, vitals are normal. Her abdomen is mildly distended and diffusely tender to palpation. A CT scan shows evidence of a fistula and strictures located in the last 30 cm of her ileum. A resection of the affected portion of the bowel is scheduled. What changes in bile metabolism are expected in this patient post-procedure?

Options:
opa. Absorption of vitamin K will not be impaired
opb. Synthesis of cholesterol in the liver will decrease
opc. The balance of the components in bile will be altered
opd. Enteric bacteria will remain the same in the small intestine
ope. Absorption of  7⍺-dehydroxylated bile will decrease
